question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 6.**
solution:
The correct answer is: because

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the use of the given words. 
 
 
• **Are made** = We use **is, am, and are **with the **third form of the verb **to make the** passive voice of a simple present tense** sentence.
 
• Were making = The **past continuous tense** is formed by combining **the past tense of to be (i.e., was/were) with the verb's present participle (-ing word).** it is often used to **describe conditions that existed in the past**. **Were **is used for a **plural subject.**
 
• Was making = The **past continuous tense** is formed by combining **the past tense of to be (i.e., was/were) with the verb's present participle (-ing word).** **Was **is used for a **singular subject.**
 
• Had made = The **past perfect simple tense** is formed by using the **auxiliary verb had together with the V3** (past participle).
 
 
 
• The given sentence is in **past continuous tense** and '**veterans**' is used, so a **plural subject always takes a plural verb.**
 
• As per the usage of the given words "were making" is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is:** "When WWII veterans were travelling, his son Michael once volunteered to take him back to Normandy."**

Hence, the correct answer is: option 2.

Complete Paragraph: *In 1945, James Leach Miller returned from World War II and shared nothing (1) about__ it with his wife. He folded up his Army (__2) uniform__, with the medals still pinned to it, and __(3) carefully__ put it in the basement, where his older boy would __(4) sometimes__ take it out to play soldiers. He never complained __(5) because__ that generation of army men didn’t air their problems. His son Michael once offered to take him back to Normandy when World War II veterans **__(6) were making__** the journey but his father shook (7)______ head saying, “I’ve been there once.” Sadly, Mr. Miller, 96 years old, (8)______ survived the bloodiest battle of World War II, died of (9)______ from the coronavirus on March 30 (10)______ an Old Soldiers’ Home.*
